claims.text: At stage-0 Đơn Hàng has 8 products, among them 'Giá đỡ laptop' at 320000 đồng; there is no product named 'Túi đựng laptop' before the file runs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql l.5-13

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, INSERT names the table, the columns being filled and a VALUES list holding one value per named column; columns left out take their default.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs INSERT reference page; §6.1 Inserting Data

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, UPDATE changes existing rows: SET names the columns and their new values, WHERE names the rows. DELETE removes whole rows selected by WHERE and has no SET clause.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §6.2 Updating Data, §6.3 Deleting Data; UPDATE and DELETE reference pages

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, WHERE is optional in UPDATE and DELETE; omitted, the statement is accepted and affects every row of the table.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §6.2 and §6.3 (without a WHERE condition all rows are updated/deleted); UPDATE, DELETE reference pages

claims.text: PostgreSQL answers a statement that returns no rows with a command tag, which psql shows under the statement: 'UPDATE n' and 'DELETE n' give the number of rows affected, and 'INSERT 0 n' gives an oid field that is always 0 followed by that number.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: libpq PQcmdStatus/command tags; SQL Command Synopses for INSERT (Outputs: INSERT oid count), UPDATE, DELETE

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, RETURNING may be added to INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE; the statement then returns the rows it wrote, including values the database computed itself such as an identity id.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §6.4 Returning Data from Modified Rows; INSERT reference page, RETURNING clause

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17 an UPDATE or DELETE affects exactly the rows its WHERE keeps, and runs without asking first. Afterwards the only undo the database itself offers is a ROLLBACK of the surrounding transaction; outside one, the statement commits on its own.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §6.2, §6.3; §7.2.2 The WHERE Clause; §3.4 Transactions (implicit BEGIN/COMMIT per statement); ROLLBACK reference page

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17 a foreign key whose declaration names no ON DELETE action defaults to NO ACTION, so a DELETE that would leave referencing rows behind raises an error; no part of that statement is applied. A declaration naming CASCADE or SET NULL makes it succeed instead.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys (NO ACTION is the default; CASCADE, SET NULL); §3.4 Transactions (a failed statement commits nothing); Error Codes 23503

claims.text: At stage-0, SELECT id, name, price_vnd FROM products WHERE price_vnd < 500000 returns 3 rows: Chuột không dây 450000, Giá đỡ laptop 320000, Đèn bàn LED 280000.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/write-basics.sql l.7 against db/seed.sql l.5-13

claims.text: products.id is declared integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, and db/seed.sql sets its sequence to 8, so the INSERT of write-basics.sql receives id 9.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/schema.sql l.4-8; db/seed.sql l.71 (setval to 8); db/queries/write-basics.sql l.10-12

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, an INSERT with RETURNING returns rows, so psql prints them as a table with a row count instead of only the INSERT command tag.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §6.4 Returning Data from Modified Rows; psql reference (a result with tuples is printed as a table with the footer row count)

claims.text: At stage-0 exactly one product is named 'Giá đỡ laptop', so a SELECT on that name answers (1 row), the UPDATE of write-basics.sql reports UPDATE 1, and the DELETE of the row just inserted reports DELETE 1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql l.5-13; db/queries/write-basics.sql l.14-19

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, ROLLBACK undoes the row changes made since BEGIN, but a value already taken from an identity sequence is not given back; the file's last line calls setval to put the sequence back to 8, and psql prints that as a one-row setval result of 8.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.17 Sequence Manipulation Functions (nextval is never rolled back); ROLLBACK reference page; db/queries/write-basics.sql l.35-37

claims.text: At stage-0, customer 1 placed orders 1, 2 and 10, so rows in orders reference customers row 1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql l.23-35 (orders 1, 2, 10 have customer_id 1)

claims.text: orders.customer_id is declared REFERENCES customers (id) with no ON DELETE rule; PostgreSQL 17's default is NO ACTION, so deleting customer 1 raises foreign_key_violation and deletes nothing.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/schema.sql l.18-24; PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.5.5 Foreign Keys (NO ACTION is the default ON DELETE action)

claims.text: A DO block with EXCEPTION WHEN foreign_key_violation catches that error; RAISE NOTICE prints its format string with % replaced by the next argument, here SQLERRM, and psql shows it as a NOTICE line, so the file continues.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §43.6.8 Trapping Errors (SQLERRM), §43.9 Errors and Messages (RAISE NOTICE), DO reference page

claims.text: After the rollback, SELECT count(*) FROM products answers 8 at stage-0, since the inserted row is gone and no seeded row was removed.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/write-basics.sql l.21, l.33 against db/seed.sql l.5-13

claims.text: Replacing line 16 of write-basics.sql with a bare ';' leaves UPDATE products SET price_vnd = 300000 with no WHERE. The INSERT above it has already added a ninth row inside the transaction, so the statement sets all 9 prices to 300000 and psql prints UPDATE 9.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/write-basics.sql l.10-16; db/seed.sql l.5-13 (8 products); PostgreSQL 17 UPDATE Outputs (count = rows updated)

claims.text: scripts/up.sh starts the lab, and scripts/sql/run-query.sh <name> runs db/queries/<name>.sql against the lab database with psql, echoing each statement.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: scripts/sql/run-query.sh l.7-11 (--echo-queries, --file); STAGE.md 'What exists at this tag'

claims.text: When a SELECT and a following UPDATE or DELETE carry the same WHERE on the same table and nothing else writes to it in between, the row count the SELECT prints is the number of rows the write will affect, so the SELECT shows the size of the change before it happens.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs UPDATE reference page (all rows that satisfy the condition); §7.2.2 The WHERE Clause
